rules.title: Network-Hosted PowerShell With Suspicious Execution Context

detection_logic.summary: Detects Sysmon Event ID 1 for PowerShell or PowerShell Core launched with a generic UNC path and at least one suspicious execution-option category.
detection_logic.sigma_yaml:
title: Network-Hosted PowerShell With Suspicious Execution Context
id: 4d2c6ef4-4a79-4d56-b6a0-ef71d64caa03
status: proposed
description: Detects PowerShell process creation from a UNC path when execution options indicate potentially suspicious noninteractive, bypass, encoded, hidden, or command-based execution.
author: Project Janus
date: 2026-08-11
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: sysmon
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_event:
    EventID: 1
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\\powershell.exe'
      - '\\pwsh.exe'
  selection_unc:
    CommandLine|contains: '\\\\'
  selection_suspicious_context:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
      - '-NonInteractive'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
  selection_noprofile_command:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-NoProfile'
      - '-Command'
  condition: selection_event and selection_image and selection_unc and (selection_suspicious_context or selection_noprofile_command)
falsepositives:
  - Approved administration scripts executed from network shares
  - Software deployment or logon scripts
  - PowerShell automation using noninteractive or execution-policy options
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized record contains data.event_id 1, a PowerShell process image, a UNC path in data.command_line, and -NoProfile, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, and -Command options.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized baseline process-creation record provides a non-PowerShell Event ID 1 example that lacks the proposed PowerShell image, UNC-path, and suspicious-option conditions.

expected_attack_result.expected_behavior: Expected to match PowerShell process creation containing a generic UNC path and suspicious execution-option categories.

expected_baseline_result.expected_behavior: Expected to produce no matches for baseline process-creation records that lack the combined PowerShell, UNC-path, and suspicious-option conditions.

limitations: This Sigma candidate detects only the process-creation component and does not establish destructive impact by itself.
Generic UNC PowerShell execution with bypass, noninteractive, encoded, hidden, or command options can be legitimate administrative activity.
Sigma field mappings and correlation behavior vary across backends.

deployment_target.description: Portable Sigma artifact; not actively deployed in the MVP

rules.title: Network-Hosted PowerShell Execution With Destructive Script Content

detection_logic.summary: Correlates network-hosted PowerShell process creation using suspicious execution options with PowerShell operational content containing destructive filesystem-operation categories on the same host within five minutes.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized process-creation record contains data.event_id 1, data.process_image ending in powershell.exe, a UNC path in data.command_line, and suspicious execution options.

evidence_references.label: attack
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized PowerShell operational record contains data.event_id 4103 and data.script_text with Remove-Item.

evidence_references.label: baseline
evidence_references.relevance: The normalized baseline PowerShell record is Event ID 4103 but its data.script_text does not contain a proposed destructive filesystem-operation category.

expected_attack_result.expected_behavior: Expected to generate a high-confidence correlation when both components occur on the same host within 300 seconds; a single matched component is expected to be assigned medium confidence.

expected_baseline_result.expected_behavior: Expected to produce no matches where baseline records do not satisfy both the network-hosted suspicious PowerShell component and destructive PowerShell-content component.

limitations: PowerShell Event IDs 4103 and 4104 depend on logging configuration and may be absent.
Host-and-time correlation can combine unrelated activity when process identifiers are unavailable across sources.
Destructive PowerShell filesystem commands and network-hosted PowerShell can be legitimate administrative or maintenance activity.
This rule does not use RDP attribution as detection proof.

deployment_target.description: Windows machine running the Project Janus Python scripts
